subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw add Mission Control workspace-wide editing and any host/system filesystem browser scope, and what authorization boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior changes which files operator clients can read or write and crosses a deliberate Gateway filesystem boundary.

options.title: Approve workspace-only next step
options.body: Keep host/system browsing out of scope and route workspace browsing/editing through a bounded agents.workspace.* design with explicit read/admin scopes, root confinement, size limits, destructive-operation UX, and real UI proof.

options.title: Keep bootstrap-only editing
options.body: Leave Mission Control editing restricted to bootstrap and memory files while allowing read-only workspace previews for non-editable inspection.

options.title: Open system-scope design
options.body: Require a separate security design for host filesystem browsing with explicit opt-in, auditing, sensitive-file handling, read/write limits, and recovery UX before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve workspace-only next step
recommendation.body: Keep host/system browsing out of scope and route workspace browsing/editing through a bounded agents.workspace.* design with explicit read/admin scopes, root confinement, size limits, destructive-operation UX, and real UI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current read-only workspace RPC boundary and are the strongest recent history signal for the file-access product/security decision.
